question:
Create a new KiCad project named b19 in the project directory and draw its schematic for the following request.

Build a battery-powered capacitive soil-moisture sensor using an ATmega328P-AU, an 8 MHz three-pin resonator, two AAA cells in series, an nRF24L01 module and an ATSHA204A single-wire authentication device. Run directly from the battery supply. Firmware uses PB1 for radio CE, PB2 for CSN, the hardware SPI pins for radio data, PC3 for ATSHA data, PD3 for probe excitation and PC0 for the sensed voltage; radio IRQ is unused.
Use the supplied one-contact capacitive-probe footprint. The sensing front end needs a 10k excitation resistor, Schottky rectifier, 1 uF integration capacitor and 510k discharge resistor. Include reset pull-up/button and FTDI auto-reset coupling, radio supply bulk capacitance, and the ATSHA pull-up. The 1x6 ISP order is MISO, battery+, SCK, MOSI, RESET, GND; FTDI order is GND, GND, battery+, MCU RX, MCU TX, DTR. Use the local probe, battery holder and radio footprints.
Local dependencies: Use the project-local footprint libraries in lib/ under the project directory (local_footprints.pretty and custom_footprints.pretty); use standard KiCad libraries for everything else.
answer:
Created the [b19 KiCad project](file:///home/andreferraz/EDA_Agent/eval/output/b19/run4/b19.kicad_pro) and its [schematic](file:///home/andreferraz/EDA_Agent/eval/output/b19/run4/b19.kicad_sch).

The requested connections and local footprints are included. ERC reports **0 errors and 22 symbol-library mismatch warnings**; the warnings remain after a library refresh.

Assumptions and checks before assembly:

- Use 2.7–3.6 V at VBAT for the 8 MHz MCU and radio; do not connect a 5 V FTDI or ISP supply.
- Confirm the radio module’s pin numbering against the supplied footprint.
- I created a project-local ATSHA204A symbol. Its pinout should be checked against the selected device datasheet.
